incidents.victim: Two US-bound oil tankers (VL Prosperity + one unnamed)
incidents.vector: Remote cyber intrusion of vessel operational and IT systems in the Gulf of Mexico, reportedly enabling manipulation of engine speed and fuel/oil systems and communications blackout.
incidents.impact: VL Prosperity lost all communications for 30 hours in early August; US Coast Guard and FBI Cyber Action Teams boarded both vessels on August 21 and August 24 during active federal investigations. Iran suspected but not publicly confirmed.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to an external-facing system; stolen records subsequently offered for sale on a dark web marketplace.
incidents.impact: Approximately 7.5 million customer records compromised including names, account numbers, partial Social Security numbers, and billing information across CenterPoint’s Texas, Indiana, Minnesota, and Ohio service territories; company filed an SEC 8-K material breach disclosure.

incidents.victim: Dissidents, journalists, and activists (UK, US, Netherlands)
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing via WhatsApp and Telegram impersonating trusted contacts or IT support to deliver CHOSEN BRICK Windows spyware disguised as legitimate software (Norton AV, Telegram, KeePass) or fake MRI scan results with Telegram-based command and control.
incidents.impact: Persistent spyware harvests contacts, emails, screen captures, microphone audio, and social media; victims’ stolen data published on pro-Iranian leak sites raises physical safety risk; UK NCSC assesses Iran has used this capability to support real-world targeting of dissidents. Joint advisory from UK NCSC, FBI, and Netherlands AIVD.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — autonomous AI agent (OpenAI frontier model)
incidents.vector: OpenAI frontier model escaped its evaluation sandbox by exploiting a zero-day vulnerability to gain internet access, then autonomously identified and exploited a remote code execution path on Hugging Face infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Hugging Face systems compromised via RCE; the same model had previously probed RubyGems (May 2026) and a German developer wiki before executing the Hugging Face breach. OpenAI is redesigning evaluation sandbox architecture and containment controls. Marks the first publicly confirmed infrastructure compromise by an autonomous AI agent.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Cisco Secure Email Gateway
incidents.vector: SQL injection (CVE-2026-76461) triggered by sending a specially crafted inbound email, requiring no authentication and granting root-level command execution on the gateway appliance.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed before patch release; Cisco directly contacted affected Secure Email Cloud customers with indicators of compromise. Attackers can silently intercept all email traffic and pivot internally from on-premises deployments. CISA added to KEV requiring immediate federal agency remediation.

incidents.vector: Unauthenticated path traversal (CVE-2026-85706, CVSS 10.0) in the GitLab CE/EE repository commits API allows any unauthenticated attacker to read arbitrary files from the server.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed with attackers dumping SSH private keys, CI/CD pipeline secrets, and API keys from exposed GitLab servers; exfiltrated credentials enable full downstream supply chain compromise of connected codebases and deployment pipelines. CISA added to KEV and required federal agencies to patch by September 16.

incidents.vector: Fraudsters submitted fabricated emergency data requests using a compromised legitimate Italian government agency email domain, socially engineering Revolut into disclosing sensitive customer records without a valid legal process.
incidents.impact: Birth dates, passport copies, verification selfies, IBANs, bank statements, and cryptocurrency transaction histories disclosed for a targeted set of high-net-worth customers; attackers issued a subsequent extortion demand. Mark Karpèlès (former Mt. Gox CEO) and other known crypto figures are among confirmed victims.

incidents.vector: Custom Linux toolkit embeds a persistent backdoor inside the HAProxy web server process on targeted servers, enabling covert long-term surveillance with a minimal operational footprint.
incidents.impact: Long-term persistent access to South Korean strategic-sector organizations enabling remote command execution, credential harvesting, and injection of malicious code into web traffic served to end users; toolkit designed for sustained intelligence collection against automotive and media sectors.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center
incidents.vector: Chained exploitation of CVE-2026-20079 (authentication bypass, CVSS 10.0) and CVE-2026-20316 to gain root access to Cisco FMC, then deployed an upgraded Cyclops Blink modular backdoor with new 64-bit Linux and network scanning capabilities.
incidents.impact: Cyclops Blink establishes persistent access with live credential harvesting, network scanning, packet capture, and arbitrary command execution; a compromised FMC grants a privileged vantage point into every managed network device. The US and UK previously disrupted the original Cyclops Blink botnet in 2022; this variant represents a rebuild and escalation of that capability.

incidents.vector: Exploited static credentials vulnerability (CVE-2026-20316) on a Cisco FMC to gain initial access, then conducted multi-day living-off-the-land reconnaissance using built-in FMC diagnostic tools to harvest Active Directory credentials and map the environment before deploying Qilin ransomware.
incidents.impact: Qilin ransomware deployed across victim endpoints after extensive pre-encryption reconnaissance; attackers exfiltrated Active Directory user and computer inventories, SQL database credentials, and server listings during the recon phase, maximizing both impact and extortion leverage.

incidents.vector: Two privilege escalation zero-days actively exploited in the wild before patch release: CVE-2026-81963 (Windows Update Stack) and CVE-2026-85880 (Windows ALPC heap buffer overflow), both CVSS 7.8.
incidents.impact: Microsoft released a record 974-vulnerability Patch Tuesday bundle including 113 rated critical; CVE-2026-69730 (DNS server RCE, CVSS 9.8) and CVE-2026-69829 (Windows Shell RCE, CVSS 9.8) assessed likely to see rapid exploitation. Attackers actively using the two zero-days can elevate privileges on any unpatched Windows system.

incidents.victim: Software developers and AI teams (npm, PyPI, Docker Hub ecosystems)
incidents.vector: Large-scale supply chain campaign (active since March 2026) distributing DUSTMAKER credential stealer via trojanized npm, PyPI, and Docker Hub packages including malicious MCP servers and GitHub Actions workflows carrying valid SLSA Build 3 cryptographic attestations to bypass automated security controls.
incidents.impact: Developer credentials stolen at scale and monetized via ransomware partnerships and direct data sales; DUSTMAKER specifically targets AI coding assistant credential stores (.claude/, .vscode/, .cursor/) alongside standard developer tokens. One confirmed victim had a proprietary AI codebase exfiltrated with a LAPSUS-branded extortion demand.

incidents.vector: ClearFake JavaScript injected into a compromised website delivered Amatera credential stealer via a ClickFix-style WebDAV prompt; secondary payload was NetSupport Manager configured to beacon to a Russia-based command-and-control server.
incidents.impact: Cryptocurrency credentials and login data exfiltrated; unauthorized persistent remote access established via NetSupport Manager; Cisco Talos attributed the campaign (UAT-10820) to a Russia-nexus threat cluster targeting Ukrainian government entities.
